findings.title: Materials' 67-point lens gap signals earnings cliff
findings.body: Materials trades at 16.09x forward but 35.38x trailing, a 55 percent compression that implies 120 percent earnings growth next year. The market is pricing a margin recovery that would be unprecedented for a sector whose trailing multiple sits at the 86th percentile of its own five-year range.

findings.title: Consumer Staples' forward price ignores trailing richness
findings.body: Consumer Staples' forward P/E of 18.61 sits at the 4th percentile while its trailing multiple of 27.23 is at the 72nd. That 68-point gap implies 46 percent earnings growth, a bet that staples can suddenly accelerate after years of stagnation — a sharp reversal from the sector's defensive reputation.

findings.title: Real Estate's month collapse outruns its multiple
findings.body: Real Estate's forward percentile fell 33 points in one month to the 6th percentile, yet its forward P/E of 33.64 remains the highest in the table. The market has repriced the sector's rank far faster than its actual earnings multiple, suggesting the selloff is about sentiment, not fundamentals.
